en: Yeah. And it's not just a guys' sport, but something the whole family can enjoy.
If I ever do move there, I wonder if I'll become a fan of my local baseball team?
That'd be nice. Baseball is definitely a sport that's part of the local scene.
Incidentally, I heard Las Vegas is getting a new ballpark. Maybe I'll go when it's finished!
That'd be awesome! Catch a game during the day and hit the casinos at night! That's the life!
I wonder if bringing pets along is allowed?
No, I'm pretty sure it isn't. I know most ballparks don't allow pets, at least.
Oh, then I wouldn't be able to bring Ulysses with me. That's a shame.
Do you have miso soup every day, Shion-chan?
Let's see... I have bread for breakfast fairly often, but I usually have miso soup at least once a day, I think.
Say, did you know miso is great for both your health and beauty?
Oh my, is it really?
Yep, it's packed with nutrients like proteins and minerals, it's a digestive aid, and has anti-cancer properties. Miso's awesome!
Oh my, I had no idea!
That's because us Japanese people take it for granted! Oh right, it's also good for your skin!
I heard eating it can help reduce the growth of freckles and other stuff, too.
You know, we use miso in most of our cooking. I wonder if that's why my mother and I are so pretty?
Hahaha! I'm sure that's it!
Speaking of which, my mother says her favorite thing about Japan is the miso.
Yeah, they don't have miso in France, do they?
That's right. Now, she loves it so much that she adds miso into her recipes for French cuisine!
Wow, what does that taste like? I'd love to try it sometime!
Oh, you know what else? I also heard that miso is great for a hangover!
Yep. It helps to purge the alcohol from your body, and prevents it from building up in your fat.
The next time I wind up drinking too much, I'll be sure to have a bowl of miso soup.
Good idea. That'll probably shake off the wooziness and help you clear your head.
I just had an idea. Maybe I should try putting some miso in Ulysses' food as well?
Huh. Is it safe for dogs to eat?
Yes, so long as there isn't too much salt in it. He hasn't been getting much water lately, so maybe I could give him a bit of miso soup to help.
Wow, you really pay attention to your pet's health, huh?
The other day, I saw a TV special about people who make miso for a living.
Needless to say, people in that line of work don't visit our club...
Yeah, I imagine they don't have much money to spare for flashy cabaret clubs.
Do you like tebasaki, Shion-chan?
I don't eat them very often, but I suppose that's because I don't frequent places that serve them. Typically, I wind up having chicken karaage instead.
Did you know the skin of the chicken wings is high in collagen?
It's full of vitamin A, too, which has anti-aging properties and strengthens bones and joints!
My, you're quite knowledgeable, Shinada-san! I may have to try some soon.
Hey, I'm a health-conscious kind of guy. And I'm always ready to share food tips!
Speaking of tebasaki, did you know they have a special version of them in America?
They're called buffalo wings. The wings are fried and then covered with a strong, spicy sauce.
They're extremely popular over there!
Wow, I've never heard of them! I kind of want to give them a try now.
That reminds me. I didn't go, but my friend had the afterparty for her wedding at a tebasaki place.
Wow, they do wedding afterparties there?
Indeed. People around here love their tebasaki, after all! Especially the men!
Oh yeah, you Nagoya folks are real big on tebasaki, aren't you?
They're also good to use for dog food.
Wow, for real?
Yes! You can serve them raw or stewed. They're apparently good for dogs. Maybe I should try feeding them to Ulysses!
I never would've thought of giving them to dogs.
You know, I've never actually been to a restaurant that specializes in tebasaki.
Whoa, really? You gotta go! If you want, I can take you to one!
Goodness, you sure know a lot about the parts of the world I don't, Shinada-san.
Hey, I'd love to go to the kinds of restaurants you usually go to, Shion-chan.
I hear the rich and famous in LA hit up ski resorts over the Christmas holiday season.
Oh my, really? I find it hard to imagine going someplace colder in the middle of winter. Why not go someplace warm, like Dubai?
Well, the West Coast is already warm year-round, so rich people like to head up into the mountains to have themselves a white Christmas.
Goodness, actively chasing after harsh weather for fun certainly sounds like the charmed celebrity lifestyle to me!
I guess it's because they never get snow normally. I'm a little jealous.
That reminds me of a ski resort in France called Courchevel.
It's also packed with high-end boutiques and caters to the rich. I'd love to go someday on a holiday.
Geez, what's the point of shopping at a ski resort? Just go there for the skiing. You rich people sure are strange, I tell ya.
Incidentally, remember my racer friend I told you about? He said his family has a private jet.
Yes. Apparently when he goes to resorts he personally pilots it to his destination!
Whoa, it's like rich people live in a totally different world.
You know, one thing I admire about wealthy Americans is their ability to own private beaches.
Private beaches!?
Yes! They buy entire islands sometimes, and get to name the beach as they like! I'd love to swim at a beach named after me!
I can understand a private villa, but a whole dang island!? I have to bust my ass just to pay rent...
Oh, did you know that our club is going to be putting on a Christmas party?
Oh wow, are you going to be here for it?
I've actually been invited to a different party, and I'd like to go to it, but my manager asked if I could work instead.
That's too bad. Maybe I can go to that party of yours for you, hehe.
But you'll be coming to the club that night, won't you, Shinada-san?
...Yes ma'am.
Tell me about the things you like, Shion-chan.
What sort of things do you mean?
Oh, I'm extremely fond of sweets!
What kinds of sweets in particular?
Let me think. I like Savarin cake, for example.
It's a cake based on a brioche dough that's baked and then soaked in simple syrup and rum. It's garnished with fruit and whipped cream.
That does sound pretty sweet. I bet you'd get heartburn from eating too much.
Also, since it's full of liquor, eating too much can also get you drunk!
Hehe, sounds like an adults-only kind of dessert. If I ever find one I'll have to try it.
Other than sweets, how about normal food?
Hmm. Miso-katsu, perhaps? I've been a big fan of those since I was a child.
I knew it. Miso-katsu is practically synonymous with Nagoya.
I suppose it's a local thing, but I was also raised with a fondness for that kind of seasoning.
After living here as long as I have, I find myself putting miso on all sorts of things besides the usual tonkatsu.
Oh my! Even here in Nagoya we don't use miso that much. Only in certain dishes.
Huh, really? But it's so tasty! I even put it in my curry and stuff.
Really now? I wouldn't have guessed you'd be a fan of something so... common.
Honestly! I don't know what sort of impression you have of me, Shinada-san, but miso-katsu is eaten by everyone!
Ahaha, sorry! I just always pictured rich people eating completely different kinds of things than regular folks.
What would you like to have more than anything?
Hmmm. Let me think.
Oh, I know. I've been looking for a pearl.
Like the gemstone? Sounds like a good gift.
Sounds pricey. I'm not sure I can afford that.
Now, now. I wasn't implying that I wanted to get one as a gift.
Huh? Then what do you want it for?
I'd like to design a pearl brooch on my own! A lot of people own the ones that are sold in shops, so I'd like one that's unique.
That's amazing. But also kind of hardcore. It'd be hard to get you a decent present after that.
What kinds of TV shows do you watch?
I... don't watch television all that much.
Because there's nothing worth watching. Every channel just shows the same old uninteresting variety shows.
That's true. They don't even broadcast baseball games any more.
I hear many people go out of their way to get cable TV so they can watch games. Perhaps it isn't so popular these days.
Until just recently, most Japanese guys would get home from work, crack open a beer, and kick back to watch the game on TV.
My father did that as well. Oh, I feel nostalgic just thinking about it.
Yeah, those were the days.
Variety shows can be interesting. There are quiz shows and educational programming too. You should check them out.
Oh my, really? I thought it was nothing but comedy.
No way. There are shows you can participate in too. You use the remote to answer the quiz, and you can even win prizes if you get them all correct.
My goodness, that sort of thing is possible now? I admit that does sound intriguing.
You bet. Although, my TV isn't nearly fancy enough to do anything like that...
What about late-night TV? There's a lot more stuff for adults than during prime time, so you can probably find some shows you like.
Oh, I can't do that. Keeping late hours would ruin my looks, so I try to get to bed early.
You could always record it. Don't you have a DVR or something like that?
I don't watch enough TV to justify owning one. If I have the time, I'd rather read.
I guess girls these days aren't into TV.
What sort of hobbies do you have, Shion-chan?
Hm. Maybe travel?
Overseas?
Yes. Conversely though, I haven't traveled around Japan much at all.
Why overseas? There's a lot of cool stuff to do in Japan as well. I'd love to go to Okinawa.
It's because I'm a fan of foreign films. I enjoy going to see locations used for movie shoots.
Wow, you're really into it.
You're a total fangirl! Like those ladies who are all into Korean pop culture.
Please refrain from lumping me in with them, would you? I'm not given to trends.
Haha, sorry.
What countries have you been to?
Let's see. I've been to several places in the United States, as well as France, Germany, and Italy. I think that's it.
That seems like a lot, even for someone who travels often.
Oh, those are just the countries related to movies. I've been to many more countries that have nothing to do with film.
Whoa, really? That's amazing. And I've never even flown business class.
You're not bored with it yet? Are there really that many famous movie locations to go to?
Actually, I hear they shoot footage on sets and combine it with CGI afterwards, so they don't do as much on-site shooting anymore.
I don't think modern movies will create as many memorable locations like older movies have done.
That's a shame. Maybe visiting movie locations won't be a thing much longer.
What do you like about it?
I love to take photos. That's my main reason to go on trips.
You take photos?
Yes. I bring an SLR with me. I'm good at taking photos with manual focus.
That's amazing. You're really hardcore.
I'll take hundreds of photos on a single trip, enough to fill an entire album! Maybe next time I can bring some for you to look at?
I'd love to see them!
Does someone take photos of you?
Depending on the location, yes. If it's a spot from a famous movie, I'll strike the same pose as the actor did in the scene!
You know, I do photography as part of my job too.  Maybe I can shoot you sometime?
Oh, would you be willing to do that? On an overseas trip together, of course!
Hey, if you're buying, let's do it!
Wait, hold on. Do I even have a passport?
Hey, Shion-chan, what do you like in terms of romance?
Hm? In what sense?
I mean, what do you look for in a man?
Oh, I see. I suppose his financial assets?
Oh, okay. So that's how it is.
It's just that I'd want a man who will let me live an unfettered lifestyle.
How much money are we talking? If a girl like you considers herself not rich enough, then what does that make me?
Money isn't everything. There are way more important things.
I know, and I don't need you to tell me that! But I still don't want a man who isn't well off!
Yikes, no need to get so angry about it. Maybe this was the wrong subject to bring up.
What else besides that? Does he need to be older or tall or something? Or hey, good at sports?
Are we talking about yourself here, Shinada-san?
